newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Nice eyes massive fax-logging market.
newsitem.headline: Nice eyes massive fax-logging market.

text.p: Israeli voice-logging equipment maker Nice Systems Ltd said on Sunday it was setting its sight on the huge market for facsimile-management systems.
"Any organisation with eight faxes or more is a customer for NiceFax," Joav Avtalion, Nice's vice president for business development, told a news conference.
NiceFax manages incoming and outgoing faxes, providing a central database for logging, querying and retrieving documents. Now completing beta tests, it is due to be launched in the next few weeks.
Avtalion would not speculate on the size of the market for NiceFax, since there are no directly competing products.

But Salomon Brothers analyst Victor Halpert said in a recent report: "NiceFax...is creating a brand new market segment that is expected to exceed the $350 million voice-recording niche over the next 18 months."
The NiceFax launch comes as the company widens it offerings in the voice-logging segment.

Nice president Benny Levin said the company's NiceLog product, which digitally records and archives phone conversations, had captured the leading market share for financial trading floors and air-traffic control applications.

He said Version 6.0 of NiceLog offers more advanced features and is targetted at call centres -- where large numbers of company representatives sell or respond to customer inquiries by telephone -- and market segments.
Market analysts expect the two new products to add substantially to Nice's revenues, which are expected to reach about $39 million this year.

"We believe Version 6.0 of the NiceLog system targeting the large call centre market as well as the launch of the NiceFax and NiceCall (a version of NiceLog for the lower end of the market) product lines should enable the company to deliver revenue growth of 60 percent year on year looking into 1997," said Lehman Brothers analyst Tim Luke in a recent report.
Analysts are looking for earnings this year of $0.73-$0.74 a share, growing to $1.24-$1.26 in 1997.
